Below tree: three horizontal blue wavy lines. Text inside circle below waves: \"RIVERBEND COUNTY\" (dark blue, uppercase).") # Message from the County Manager The proposed budget for fiscal year 2026-27 totals $121.5 million, an increase of 7.2 percent over the current adopted budget of $113.3 million. It protects core services, puts more money into road and bridge maintenance, and adds to the capital reserve. Property tax rates are unchanged for the third year in a row. # Budget Highlights . Road and bridge maintenance rises to $12.5 million, up from $11.2 million. . Public Safety receives $33.2 million, including funding for six new deputy positions. . The capital reserve contribution grows from $5.2 million to $6.4 million. . Debt service stays flat at $9.5 million. Key dates Public hearing: Tuesday, April 14, 2026, 6:00 PM, County Administration Building, Room 210 Budget adoption vote: Tuesday, May 5, 2026 Written comments are due by April 30, 2026. To read the complete proposed budget document, [click here.](https://www.example.org/riverbend/budget-2026) # Where the Money Goes Road and bridge maintenance is a priority in the proposed budget. Spending has risen every year since FY2022 and is proposed to reach $12.5 million in FY2027, up from $8.1 million five years earlier. Road and bridge maintenance spending Figure 1. Road and bridge maintenance spending, FY2022 to FY2027 (proposed), in millions of dollars. ![14 $12.5M Millions of dollars 12 $10.8M $11.2M 10 $8.9M $9.4M $8.1M 8 6 4 2 0 FY22 FY23 FY24 FY25 FY26 FY27 (proposed)](figures/2.1 "Bar chart. Y-axis label: \"Millions of dollars\". Y-axis ticks: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. X-axis categories: FY22, FY23, FY24, FY25, FY26, FY27 (proposed). Bars and value labels: - FY22: $8.1M (blue bar). - FY23: $8.9M (blue bar). - FY24: $9.4M (blue bar). - FY25: $10.8M (blue bar). - FY26: $11.2M (blue bar). - FY27 (proposed): $12.5M (orange bar).") ```chart {"type":"bar","data":{"labels":["FY22","FY23","FY24","FY25","FY26","FY27 (proposed)"],"datasets":[{"label":"Millions of dollars","data":[8.1,8.9,9.4,10.8,11.2,12.5],"backgroundColor":["#2f5f8a","#2f5f8a","#2f5f8a","#2f5f8a","#2f5f8a","#d0812a"]}]},"options":{"scales":{"y":{"min":0,"max":14,"title":{"display":true,"text":"Millions of dollars"},"ticks":{"stepSize":2}}}}} ``` ![](figures/2.2 "Horizontal decorative wavy line spanning left to right. - Color gradient transitions from teal/green on the left to blue/purple on the right. - No labels, axes, units, numbers, or legend.") # Spending by Department Public Safety remains the largest share of proposed spending at 27.3 percent, followed by Public Works and Roads at 22.7 percent and Health and Human Services at 19.6 percent. # Proposed FY2026-27 spending by department Figure 2. Share of proposed FY2026-27 spending by department. ![5.3% 7.8% 27.3% Public Safety 10.0% Public Works and Roads Health and Human Services 7.3% Parks and Libraries Administration Debt Service Capital Reserve 19.6% 22.7%](figures/2.3 "Pie chart titled by context: “Figure 2. Department FY2025-26 adopted FY2026-27 proposed Change

Amounts are in millions of dollars. Change is measured against the FY2025-26 adopted budget. Questions about this summary may be directed to the Office of Management and Budget at (312) 555-0142 or budget@riverbend.example.

Summary.valueString: Riverbend County’s Fiscal Year 2026-27 Proposed Budget Summary (released March 2026) outlines a $121.5 million proposed budget, up 7.2% from the $113.3 million adopted budget, emphasizing protection of core services, increased road and bridge maintenance, and a larger capital reserve contribution while keeping property tax rates unchanged; it lists key public input and adoption dates, shows spending trends and departmental shares, and provides an appendix table of adopted vs. proposed amounts by department with contact information for questions.

current adopted budget of $113.3 million. It protects core services, puts more money into road and bridge
maintenance, and adds to the capital reserve. Property tax rates are unchanged for the third year in a row.

. Public Safety receives $33.2 million, including funding for six new deputy positions.
. The capital reserve contribution grows from $5.2 million to $6.4 million.
. Debt service stays flat at $9.5 million.
